title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Modern cell-based assays for biomedical research: from conventional methods to AI-driven high content analysis.
authors: Venkataramaiah C
abstract: In vitro cell-based assays are fundamental tools in biomedical research, supporting investigations of cellular physiology, disease mechanisms, drug discovery, toxicology, regenerative medicine, and precision therapeutics. However, conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell culture models often fail to recapitulate the structural complexity and physiological functions of native tissues, prompting the development of advanced platforms, including three-dimensional (3D) cultures, organoids, organ-on-a-chip technologies, and microphysiological systems. Recent advances in cell viability and cytotoxicity assessment, functional cellular analysis, molecular profiling, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based functional genomics, high-content imaging, flow cytometry, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and automated high-throughput screening have expanded the analytical capabilities of cell-based assays. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image analysis and computational biology has enhanced cellular phenotyping, biomarker discovery, and mechanistic investigation, with the potential to improve the prediction of therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. Nevertheless, challenges related to physiological relevance, technical variability, inadequate standardization, high operational costs, scalability, poor reproducibility, cell-line misidentification, batch-to-batch variation, and inconsistent reporting continue to hinder translational applications. Future progress will depend on integrating physiologically relevant models with AI-driven analytics, spatial multi-omics, digital pathology, automated screening, and microphysiological systems. Standardized protocols, harmonized reporting practices, and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to improve reproducibility, strengthen regulatory acceptance, advance precision medicine, and reduce reliance on animal experimentation. In this context, this review critically evaluates conventional and emerging in vitro cell-based assays, emphasizing their biological principles, analytical capabilities, translational applications, and practical limitations, while highlighting future opportunities to improve predictive accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical translation.

title: Engineering copper homeostasis for microenvironment-adaptive therapy in inflammation-driven disorders.
authors: Ding F, Liu J, Liu M, Huang H, Tang H, Zhong J, Liu C, Liu Z
abstract: Inflammation-driven disorders (IDDs) arise from distinct initiating events, yet many persist because immune activation, oxidative and metabolic stress, regulated cell death, and tissue remodeling form self-reinforcing local niches. Copper connects these processes through its roles as a cuproenzyme cofactor, redox-active species and dynamically trafficked regulatory metal. Its therapeutic significance, however, is determined by disease stage, cell type, subcellular distribution and chemical state. Copper deficiency, excess or mislocalization may therefore be adaptive, protective or pathogenic in different contexts. This review develops a disease- and copper-state-specific framework that links copper homeostasis to therapeutic platform design. We first examine inflammation-associated remodeling of copper trafficking and compare representative copper states in autoimmune joint disease, metabolic inflammation, fibrosis, inflammation-associated cancer and infection-associated tissue repair. We then critically evaluate copper-dependent and copper-sensitive mechanisms governing inflammatory mediator availability, immune-cell programming and checkpoint regulation, regulated cell death, angiogenesis and stromal remodeling, while distinguishing direct mechanistic evidence from model-dependent inference. Building on this analysis, we compare pharmacological modulators with nanocarriers, copper-containing active materials and local copper-sequestering platforms that implement copper chelation or sequestration, controlled copper delivery or release, intracellular redistribution, and catalytic activation or nanozyme-like redox regulation. We further outline how pathological copper pools, activation cues, release kinetics, speciation, biodistribution and target engagement should be measured so that precision is demonstrated rather than inferred from material composition. This framework positions copper modulation as a context-specific complement to existing therapy and defines the mechanistic, analytical and translational evidence required for microenvironment-adaptive treatment of IDDs.

title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
authors: Liu B, Wei N, Liang L, Shi Z, Liu P, Zeng T, Zhang H, Zhang H
abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

title: A ratiometric dual-modal photoacoustic and near-infrared fluorescence probe for in vivo spatiotemporal mapping of butyrylcholinesterase in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Meng Y, Wang C, Hu Y, Zhou H, Zhou J, Gao W, Xing W, Shu X
abstract: Butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) is a critical biomarker for the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology; however, real-time visualization of its dynamic activity changes in deep biological tissues remains highly challenging. Herein, we report the development of BChE-PA, a novel hemicyanine-based dual-modal probe for the ratiometric detection of BChE through integrated near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence and photoacoustic (PA) imaging. The probe design utilizes a specific cyclopropanecarbonyl recognition moiety that effectively masks the internal charge transfer (ICT) process of the fluorophore. Enzymatic cleavage of the cyclopropanecarbonyl group by BChE restores the ICT effect and extends the molecular π-conjugation, triggering a significant 93 nm bathochromic shift in absorption (from 622 nm to 715 nm) and a dramatic NIR fluorescence "turn-on" response. BChE-PA exhibits an exceptional detection limit of 0.03 U/mL and high selectivity over competing esterases. By leveraging the ratiometric PA signal (PA755/PA680), we successfully performed self-calibrating, deep-tissue mapping of elevated BChE levels in the brains of APP/PS1 transgenic mice. This dual-modal platform provides a robust tool for the spatiotemporal tracking of BChE, bridging the gap between molecular environmental surveillance and clinical neuroimaging.

title: A novel deep learning-based peak detection technique for in vivo metabolite analysis of triterpenoids from Eleutherococcus senticosus leaves in Parkinson's disease mice.
authors: Wen T, Guan W, Xu S, Yang X, Li Y, Wang H, Jiang P, Chen Q
abstract: To address the challenges in mass spectrometry data processing, including poor detection of low-abundance metabolites, severe noise interference, and the reliance on labor-intensive parameter tuning in conventional peak detection methods, a deep learning-based peak detection algorithm termed MSPeakNet was developed. The model used a multi-scale convolutional module and a U-net encoder-decoder architecture integrated with an attention mechanism, enabling high-precision peak identification and noise reduction in complex biological matrices. MSPeakNet achieved precision and F1 scores comparable to CWT, with superior noise robustness, while maintaining competitive recall. The developed method was subsequently applied to the in vivo metabolite profiling of total triterpenoids from Eleutherococcus senticosus leaves (ESLT) in an MPTP-induced mouse model of Parkinson's disease (PD) using UPLC-Q-TOF/MS analysis. A total of 143 ESLT-related compounds, comprising 88 prototypes and 55 metabolites, were identified in plasma, urine, feces, and brain tissue, of which 16 prototypes were detected in brain tissue. Pharmacodynamic evaluation further confirmed that ESLT significantly ameliorated MPTP-induced motor dysfunction and dopaminergic neuronal loss. Comparative analysis further revealed distinct profiles of ESLT-related differential compounds between PD model and normal mice across multiple biological matrices; 14, 9, 6, and 4 differential metabolites were identified in feces, urine, plasma, and brain, respectively, suggesting that disease status may affect the biotransformation, distribution, and elimination of ESLT constituents. A robust and efficient deep learning-based approach for mass spectrometry peak detection was thereby established, and critical experimental evidence was provided for the discovery of anti-Parkinsonian active ingredients and quality markers from E. senticosus leaves.

title: Serrated Pathway-Related Post-Colonoscopy Colorectal Cancer　Detected During Surveillance Colonoscopy: A Case Report.
authors: Hadatsuki H, Ichijima R, Mizuguchi Y, Toyoshima N, Okita H, Haga T, Kumamoto Y, Tsukamoto S
abstract: Post-colonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) remains a critical clinical challenge, and sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) are important precursor lesions. We report a case of advanced transverse colon cancer suspected to be associated with the serrated pathway that was detected during periodic surveillance colonoscopy. An 82-year-old male had undergone periodic surveillance colonoscopy after curative resection via endoscopic submucosal dissection for rectosigmoid intramucosal cancer. Colonoscopy revealed a type 2 advanced tumor near the hepatic flexure and multiple serrated lesions throughout the colon, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for serrated polyposis syndrome (SPS). Immunohistochemistry showed deficient mismatch repair with loss of MLH1 and PMS2, and molecular analysis revealed BRAF V600E and KRAS mutations. The patient underwent robot-assisted transverse colectomy, and pathological staging was pT3N0. He remains recurrence-free 6 months after surgery. This case highlights the difficulty of distinguishing between a missed serrated lesion and a newly developed cancer in serrated pathway-related PCCRC. In patients with multiple SSLs or SPS, high-quality colonoscopy, recognition of SPS criteria, complete resection of detectable serrated lesions, and individualized surveillance strategies may be essential for the prevention and early detection of PCCRC.

title: Anti-inflammatory effects of the injectable hydrogen-releasing material Mg2Si on rheumatoid foot.
authors: Tian P, Zhang L, Cheng Y, Lu C, Ding X, Wan H
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune inflammatory disease that typically affects multiple symmetrical joints, particularly the foot. To date, the intricate pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis remains elusive, with a primary hallmark being increased oxidative stress and excessive production of reactive oxygen species. Molecular hydrogen, which can selectively scavenge hydroxyl radicals, has been widely used to treat inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis. However, traditional hydrogen delivery strategies struggle to maintain high concentrations, significantly compromising the therapeutic efficacy of rheumatoid arthritis. As a new type of micro-nano material, magnesium silicide (Mg2Si) generates high concentrations of hydrogen after local injection. In this study, Mg2Si was locally injected into the ankle joints of collagen-induced arthritis rats to observe the ameliorative effect of Mg2Si on arthritis in rats with rheumatoid foot. Compared with the blank control group, the model group presented increased inflammation according to the arthritis score, inflammatory factor level, and various clinical examinations, including pathology, ultrasound, digital radiography, and micro-computed tomography. In contrast, after treatment with molecular hydrogen, which was released by Mg2Si, the arthritis symptoms of rats with rheumatoid foot were significantly alleviated. As a novel micro-nanomaterial, Mg2Si can maintain a high concentration of hydrogen after local injection. The above results suggest that the molecular hydrogen released by Mg2Si have anti-inflammatory effects on rheumatoid arthritis, which opens up a new approach for the clinical treatment of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Transrectal ultrasonographic assessment of the equine fetal distal limb beyond the first phalanx for predicting fetal age and bone development in Quarter Horses.
authors: Renaudin C, Wensley F, Morgan J, Cassano J, Spriet M
abstract: In Quarter Horses (QH), fetal age can be predicted within 2 weeks prior to 200- days of gestation ultrasonographically; however, as pregnancy advances, accuracy decreases. Recently, fetal ultrasonographic measurement of the first phalanx length (P1L) was introduced as a novel biometric parameter during late gestation, and the timing of appearance and closure of P1 epiphyses has been identified as potential markers of bone development. The overall aim of this study is to describe distal limb bone development beyond the first phalanx. Ten healthy pregnant mares (9 QH and 1 Thoroughbred carrying a QH fetus) with known ovulation dates were used. Transrectal ultrasonography was performed every 2 weeks from 9 months of gestation until parturition. P2 length (P2L) correlated highly with days of gestation (p < 0.0001; r2 = 0.75). A correlation equation was established: y = 5.343 (±0.403) x +205.1(±6.99) (y = predicted value of gestational age in days; x = P2 length in mm). Ossification of distal MC3, P1 and P2 epiphyses, and sesamoid bones, appeared in a chronological order, with the distal MC3 epiphysis ossification center appearing first, followed by distal P1, distal P2, proximal sesamoid bones, and finally distal sesamoid bone. Distal limb ossification can be considered complete in QH when the distal MC3 epiphysis, proximal epiphyses of P1 and P2, and all sesamoid bones are present. Clinically, fetal ultrasonography of the distal limb may be used to assess fetal age and bone development.

title: Dynamical mechanisms of pathological phase-amplitude coupling in a network comprising subthalamic and two types of globus pallidus neurons.
authors: Yang J, Shi X, Wang L
abstract: Pathologically enhanced β oscillations and their cross-frequency coupling with high-frequency oscillations is a hallmark of Parkinson's disease, yet its dynamical origins remain elusive, partly due to oversimplified modeling of the GPe as a homogeneous nucleus. In this study, we developed a biophysical STN-heterogeneous GPe network model incorporating prototypic (TI) and arkypallidal (TA) neurons to investigate the phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) generation and the differential roles of intra-loop pathways. Our results show that the STN-TI-STN sub-loop serves as the core dynamical substrate for generating and sustaining pathological PAC. TA neurons do not drive PAC but potentiate it via lateral inhibition onto TI, with their drive originating from STN input. Selective TI excitation abolishes PAC, whereas TA stimulation is ineffective. The consistent evolution of synchronization index, β power, and modulation index supports PAC as a reliable feedback biomarker. This work points to a new network mechanism of PAC generation within the STN-heterogeneous GPe network, identifies the TI subpopulation as a promising target for precision optogenetic intervention, and provides theoretical foundations for developing adaptive DBS strategies guided by PAC-based feedback signals.

title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
authors: Xing Y, Gao Y, Hong Z, Tian C, Cai H, Chu H, Yang Y, Liang PY
abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

title: A versatile multi-dimensional ratiometric sensor exploiting material-interface properties for t-Tau protein detection in human serum.
authors: Yuan W, Jin Q, Rong R, Wang X, Wang X, Wang X
abstract: Ratiometric sensor provides self-calibration for enhanced reliability, but conventional single-ratio designs are validated only under fixed instrumental conditions, making their reliability environment-dependent and inherently non-transferable to other analytical scenarios. Herein, we exploited the physical, chemical and interfacial changes inherent to sensor fabrication to extract multiple orthogonal signals from a single interface, constructing a versatile multi-dimensional ratiometric sensor that simultaneously enhanced accuracy and scenario adaptability. As proof of concept, this sensor was applied to detect total tau protein (t-Tau), a key Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarker. Electrospun Fe-MOF/polyacrylonitrile nanofibers on a glassy carbon electrode served as the substrate, providing a stable redox peak current (Ip) and a photothermal temperature signal (T) as intrinsic references. Target recognition triggered a catalytic hairpin assembly that released a Ru-MOF-labeled probe, generating dynamic electrochemiluminescence (IECL) and charge-transfer resistance (Rct) responses. After blank correction, the dynamic signals were integrated with the two references to yield five independent ratiometric outputs (ΔRct/Ip, ΔRct/ΔT, ΔRct/ΔIECL, ΔIECL/ΔT, ΔIECL/Ip), all exhibiting detection limits (3.4-4.1 fg mL-1) three orders of magnitude below the AD diagnostic threshold (21.3 pg mL-1). This demonstrated each ratio as an independently valid strategy for flexible deployment across varied scenarios. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis confirmed robust discriminatory power across all five ratios (area under the ROC curve 0.80-0.95), enabling both mutual cross-validation among outputs and flexible selection of the optimal ratio for available instrumentation. Collectively, by exploiting material-interface properties, this work provided a versatile platform for accurate biomarker detection adaptable to diverse analytical scenarios and laboratory settings.

title: Circulating LRG1 in heart failure: association with type 2 diabetes and antidiabetic therapy class.
authors: Alrosan K, Odeh M, Alqudah A, Abudalo R, Qnais E
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist and share remodelling and inflammatory mechanisms. Although leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) has been identified as a biomarker associated with vascular remodelling, fibrosis, and inflammation, its role in HF patients with type 2 diabetes and its connection to antidiabetic treatments remains unclear. METHODS: 115 patients with HF were divided into three groups for this cross-sectional study: HF who had no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and were not receiving antidiabetic medication at enrolment (n = 42), HF with T2DM treated with DPP-4 inhibitors (n = 35), and HF with T2DM treated with SGLT-2 inhibitors (n = 38). The groups' clinical characteristics, metabolic parameters, and circulating LRG1 levels were compared. RESULTS: LRG1 levels differed significantly across the groups (p = 0.002), with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. A post hoc analysis revealed a significant difference between the SGLT-2 inhibitor group and group of no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (p = 0.001). No significant correlations were observed between LRG1 and clinical or metabolic variables. CONCLUSION: Circulating LRG1 levels in HF patients differed between study groups, with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. These findings suggest an association between treatment group and LRG1 levels, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the effects of antidiabetic medications on inflammatory and remodelling pathways.

title: Multiple Rectal Neuroendocrine Tumors Treated by Endoscopic Resection: A Case Report.
authors: Matsuki H, Ichijima R, Sekiguchi M, Toyoshima N, Kawamura R, Mizuguchi Y, Takamaru H, Yamada M
abstract: Rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are typically solitary, and the occurrence of multiple lesions is uncommon. We present a case of multiple rectal NETs in a 41-year-old man. Colonoscopy performed at another hospital revealed three lesions (4 mm in the sigmoid colon and 5 and 10 mm in the rectum), all of which were diagnosed as NET, grade 1 (G1), following endoscopic resection; one lesion had a positive vertical margin. Upon referral to our institution, repeat colonoscopy demonstrated multiple yellowish, slightly elevated lesions throughout the rectum, all of which were histologically confirmed as NETs. Imaging studies showed no evidence of lymph node or distant metastasis. Although additional surgical resection was considered because of the multiplicity of lesions and positive margin, the patient strongly preferred endoscopic therapy. Eight lesions were successfully resected using endoscopic mucosal resection with a cap or endoscopic submucosal dissection. Histopathological examination revealed seven NET, G1 lesions and one NET, G2 lesion. Additional surgery was recommended but was declined by the patient, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis has been observed during 18 months of follow-up. This rare case highlights the potential role and the limitations of endoscopic treatment in patients with multiple rectal NETs.

title: Multi-Loop Traction Device-Assisted Papillary Traction During Single-Balloon Enteroscopy-Assisted Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography After Roux-en-Y Gastrectomy: A Four-Case Series.
authors: Hirata D, Komoto S, Horiuchi T, Yoshioka M, Takahashi S, Furuhashi H, Narimatsu K, Hokari R
abstract: Biliary cannulation during single-balloon enteroscopy-assisted endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography after Roux-en-Y gastrectomy can remain challenging even after the papilla is reached. Unfavorable papillary orientation, tangential visualization, and excessive papillary mobility can impair alignment with the bile duct axis. We used a multi-loop traction device (MLTD; Boston Scientific Japan, Tokyo, Japan) as an adjunct for papillary traction in four patients with Roux-en-Y anatomy after gastrectomy. The indications were suspected distal bile duct cancer in one patient and common bile duct stones in three patients. An SIF-H290S enteroscope (Olympus Medical Systems Corp., Tokyo, Japan) was used in all patients. After MLTD traction, biliary cannulation and the intended diagnostic or therapeutic intervention were completed in all four cases. No procedure-related adverse events were observed during hospitalization or through the first outpatient visit after discharge. Traction corrected the papillary axis in papillae facing the blind limb and stabilized highly mobile papillae. MLTD-assisted papillary traction may serve as a practical rescue technique when difficult cannulation results from unfavorable papillary orientation or excessive mobility.

title: Engineered microorganisms drive local metabolic reprogramming to Re-educate systemic immunity.
authors: Ma Y, Yang Y, Yu Z, Jin M, Jin Y, Wang J, Wang H, Zhao Q
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

title: Long-term Endoscopic Evolution of a Pyloric Gland Adenoma Arising in Nonatrophic Gastric Mucosa and Initially Resembling a Fundic Gland Polyp.
authors: Kobayashi R, Nakanishi H, Takaura K, Tanaka S, Maeyashiki C, Tamaki N, Yasui Y, Sakurai U
abstract: Pyloric gland adenoma (PGA) is a rare gastric epithelial neoplasm often associated with autoimmune or metaplastic atrophic gastritis. An 80-year-old man underwent serial upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. A small gastric fundus lesion initially resembling a fundic gland polyp (FGP) was followed without biopsy. Over 11 years, it enlarged to 22 mm and became increasingly whitish, against a background described endoscopically as nonatrophic. Biopsy suggested PGA, and the lesion was resected en bloc by endoscopic submucosal dissection. Closely packed pyloric-type glands showed elongation, tortuosity, branching, and cystic dilatation, with diffuse MUC6 expression and MUC5AC expression restricted to the surface epithelium. The lesion was diagnosed as PGA with low-grade dysplasia. The adjacent oxyntic mucosa showed no atrophy, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, or nodular enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia. Without an initial biopsy, whether the lesion was already PGA or developed within a pre-existing FGP remains unknown. An enlarging or increasingly whitish FGP-like lesion warrants histologic assessment, even in nonatrophic gastric mucosa.

title: Young children engage in choice-relative moral reasoning.
authors: Waltzer T, Heyman GD, Leslie AM, Levine S
abstract: A central challenge in moral reasoning is evaluating actions not only by their outcomes, but also by the alternatives that were available at the time of choice. The present study examined whether preschool-age children engage in this form of choice-relative moral reasoning. Using a child-friendly version of the trolley problem, 3- to 5-year-old children (N = 124, 51% girls) judged a protagonist who moved a barrier to protect three children's cookies from being eaten by a mean squirrel. Children typically judged this action as morally good when no better alternative was available, even when it caused harm to another child. However, they judged the same action as morally bad when a non-harmful alternative was available but not chosen. These findings suggest that preschool-age children evaluate actions in light of available alternatives rather than solely on the basis of outcomes. Thus, even young children appear to consider what else could have been done when making moral judgments.

title: Do parental questions and gestures support executive functions in toddlers born preterm and full-term?
authors: Yılmaz B, Göksun T
abstract: This study examined parental questions and gestures in the development of executive functions (EF) in preterm (PT) and full-term (FT) toddlers. Sixty-four Turkish-speaking parent-child dyads (32 girls, Mage = 26.1 months, SD = 1.33, 25 PT) were observed in free-play sessions. The form (i.e., WH, yes/no) and function (i.e., pedagogical, information-seeking, rhetorical) of parental questions and gestures accompanying them were coded. Children's working memory and cognitive flexibility skills were measured using Hide the Pots and Reverse Categorization (pre- and post-switch) tasks, respectively. Results showed that PT and FT children had similar EF skills. Parental WH questions were associated with PT children's working memory skills. Parental WH questions, not pedagogical ones, were related to children's cognitive flexibility skills, regardless of neonatal status. When accompanied by gestures, both WH and pedagogical questions were associated with PT children's working memory and cognitive flexibility skills. These results highlight the importance of specific parental input as a function of children's neonatal status in the development of EFs.

title: Early self-regulation in context: Multidimensional organization of neonatal non-nutritive sucking and its association with subclinical maternal depressive traits.
authors: Faré O, Silvestri V, Morniroli D, Petrelli A, Colombo L, Giannì ML, Bulf H
abstract: From the very first days of life, infants' affective regulation unfolds within a dyadic co-regulatory system shaped by caregiver responsivity. In contexts of reduced maternal availability, such as maternal depressive states, infants may be required to compensate for diminished interpersonal regulation by increasingly relying on their internal resources. Neonatal non-nutritive sucking (NNS) represents one of the earliest spontaneously available regulatory behaviors, contributing to physiological and behavioral homeostasis from birth. However, it remains unclear whether its spontaneous organization is associated with early relational vulnerability indexed by maternal depressive symptoms. The present study aimed to characterize the spontaneous organization of NNS in a sample of newborns (N = 42) and to examine whether individual differences in NNS are associated with maternal postnatal depressive subclinical traits measured using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Results from an exploratory principal component analysis indicated that neonatal sucking behavior was organized along two functional dimensions, reflecting overall sucking effort and behavioral activation, and the temporal organization of sucking bursts. Importantly, higher maternal depressive traits, though subclinical, were selectively associated with increased sucking effort, with infants of mothers reporting higher depressive traits showing more frequent and intense sucking, while no differences emerged for the organizational dimension. Overall, these findings suggest that individual differences in maternal depressive traits within the subclinical range may be associated with neonatal NNS effort, a precocious compensatory mobilization of regulatory resources, potentially serving both to support autonomous regulation and to elicit maternal engagement.

title: Accuracy of parent and teacher reports of early math skills.
authors: King YA, Zippert EL, Ellis A, O'Rear C, Lin J, Purpura DJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: It is important for parents and teachers to understand preschooler's early mathematics skills to best provide appropriate mathematics support. Comparing parents' and teachers' accuracy in reporting children's mathematics skills may help to ensure developmentally appropriate early math support in home and classroom environments. AIM: The present study examined the accuracy of parents' and teachers' reports of preschoolers' early mathematics skills (i.e., counting, numeral identification, and quantitative and spatial word knowledge). SAMPLE: Participants included 117 children 3 to 5 years old (M = 4.27, SD = .63, 49.6 % female) and their parent and Head Start teacher. METHOD: Parents and teachers completed surveys reporting on each child's understanding of mathematics concepts via items from different mathematics measures. Children were directly assessed on their mathematics skills via the same or similar items. RESULTS: Generally, parents' and teachers' reports were positively associated with direct assessments of children's mathematics skills. Parents' and teachers' reports of children's mathematical skills ranged from 47 % to 75 % accurate, and parents were more accurate than teachers in reporting children's quantitative word knowledge. The direction of inaccuracies (over-or underestimation) varied by mathematics skill type, such that caregivers tended to overestimate children's numeracy skills and underestimate their mathematical language knowledge. CONCLUSION: Future research is needed to examine how the accuracy of parents and teachers reports influences early mathematics development, and how potentially improving caregiver accuracy might support children's mathematics learning.

title: Parent-child facial expression recognition: the role of familiarity in interactive contexts.
authors: Palmer K, Buttle HM, Kohler M, Fong FTK, Nelson NL
abstract: The ability to express and understand emotion is fundamental to social communication, and develops through early parent-child interactions. Across two studies, we examined parents' and children's recognition of emotional expressions during a structured interactive task. In Study 1, parent-child dyads (N = 33, children aged 4-9 years) took turns producing facial expressions in response to emotion-eliciting objects while their partner guessed the eliciting object. Videos of children were shown to naïve adult raters (N = 88) completing the same task. Study 1 provided initial evidence for a familiarity effect, with parents outperforming naïve raters at recognising their child's expressions. Study 2 (N = 45 dyads, children aged 4-12 years) extended this by testing whether recognition accuracy reflects familiarity with a specific partner or general parenting experience. Participants completed the task with each other and with videos of unfamiliar partners. Naïve parents (N = 69) and non-parents (N = 68) also rated the children's expressions. Study 2 confirmed a bidirectional familiarity advantage: both parents and children were more accurate with their familiar partner than with unfamiliar individuals, suggesting the effect is specific to the parent-child relationship rather than reflecting a general ability to read adult or child faces. Recognition accuracy was not strongly predicted by age, suggesting familiarity may account for more variance in performance than developmental changes in expressive clarity alone. These findings support the view that the unique parent-child bond plays a meaningful role in emotional understanding.

title: Dual-mode colorimetric sensing of bilirubin using a PDDA@peroxomolybdate composite: A spectrophotometric platform and cost-effective cotton-swab sensor for point-of-care testing.
authors: Avan AA, Filik H, Kucur M, Cabıoğlu N
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: In this work, the synthesis and characterization of a poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA)@peroxomolybdate composite are presented for the development of a dual-mode colorimetric sensing platform for point-of-care bilirubin (BLR) detection. The platform combines a laboratory-based spectrophotometric assay with a smartphone-assisted cotton-swab sensor, enabling versatile and accessible screening. The spectrophotometric mode exhibited a wide linear detection range of 0.1-4.5 mg/dL (1.72-77.0 μM) and a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.032 mg/dL (0.54 μM). In parallel, the smartphone-based assay, utilizing normalized red-channel intensity values, demonstrated a broader linear range of 0.1-9.0 mg/dL (1.72-154 μM) with an LOD of 0.046 mg/dL (0.78 μM). This dual-mode sensing approach offers flexibility by letting users choose between the high analytical accuracy of laboratory instrumentation and the convenience of wide-range, on-site screening, depending on clinical requirements. Furthermore, the selectivity of the platform was comprehensively evaluated, and its practical applicability was successfully validated using adult and neonatal blood serum samples. The results highlight the strong potential of the proposed platform for reliable clinical monitoring of BLR levels.

SVIP knockdown alters UPS protein expression in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells.
authors: Kipel Ş, Çayli S, Aktaş Gİ, Nakkaş H
abstract: Testicular tumours are the most common malignant tumors in men between the ages of 15-34. Approximately 95% of testicular tumors arise from germ cells. Small VCP-interacting protein (SVIP) is a protein that regulates its function and autophagy by binding to p97/VCP, which is involved in protein degradation associated with the endoplasmic reticulum. Recent studies on SVIP have shown that SVIP is an androgen-sensitive protein. The development of secondary sex characteristics is influenced by androgens, which are significant steroid hormone. Androgens also initiate and maintain spermatogenesis in the male reproductive system. Mutations of androgen receptors are often seen in patients with disorders of male reproductive development and can cause male infertility. Studies are showing that the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) in the male reproductive system affects fertility. Therefore, investigating the expressions of USP26 and UXT, which are components of the UPS, is important for testicular biology. The expressions of SVIP, AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT were analysed by immunofluorescence, western blot and q RT-PCR method to determine the expressions of SVIP and the UPS proteins that it interacts in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells (CRL-2073) and to see the effects of suppressed SVIP expression on other proteins after SVIP siRNA transfection. At SVIP siRNA applied CRL-2073 cells, SVIP, AR, USP26 and Ubiquitin expressions decreased, while UXT expression increased, according to immunofluorescence and western blot results. According to the qRT-PCR results, SVIP gene expression decreased and AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT gene expressions increased in the group given SVIP siRNA. As a result, this study demonstrated the expression of SVIP and its interacting UPS proteins in CRL-2073 cells for the first time, making an unique and significant contribution to the literature.

title: Clinical characteristics and maternal whole-exome sequencing findings in patients with recurrent oocyte, zygote, and early embryo maturation arrest: a single-center experience.
authors: Kahraman S, Cetinkaya M, Cetinkaya CP, Madjunkova S, Kara B, Ayaz A, Aktoz F
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical phenotype, cumulative assisted reproductive technology (ART) experience, and maternal whole-exome sequencing (WES) findings in patients with recurrent Oocyte, Zygote, and Early Embryo Maturation Arrest (OZEMA), and to assess the contribution of phenotype-guided genomic evaluation in this clinically challenging population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study conducted in a fertility clinic within a general private hospital equipped with an in‑house genetic laboratory. SUBJECTS: A total of 115 females with a history of OZEMA were included, all of whom presented to the ART clinic. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The distribution of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in established OZEMA-associated genes, variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in established genes, monoallelic variants in established autosomal recessive genes, and exploratory candidate-gene findings. ART outcomes were described according to whether a prioritized WES finding was reported. RESULTS: The mean female age was 33.47 +/- 4.37 years, with a median infertility duration of 6.0 years (range, 1.0-21.0). Patients had experienced recurrent OZEMA across multiple ART cycles (median, 4; range, 1-16). Parental consanguinity was observed in 37 of 115 cases (32.2 %). Prioritized maternal WES findings were identified in 64 of 115 patients (55.7 %): 12 patients (10.4 %) had P/LP variants in established genes with genotypes consistent with the reported inheritance pattern, 17 (14.8 %) had VUS in established genes, 15 (13.0 %) had monoallelic variants in established autosomal recessive genes without a second relevant allele, and 20 (17.4 %) had exploratory candidate-gene findings. No prioritized WES finding was identified in 51 patients (44.3 %). CONCLUSIONS: Phenotype-guided maternal WES identified established P/LP findings with inheritance-consistent support in a clinically meaningful subset of patients with recurrent OZEMA and revealed a broader spectrum of additional genomic findings. These results support genomic evaluation, while the clinical interpretation of VUS, monoallelic findings in recessive genes, and exploratory candidate-gene findings should remain evidence-based.

title: Duration of post-ovulation uterine fluid in mares with persistent mating-induced endometritis predicts pregnancy rate, and earlier mating shifts fluid persistence relative to ovulation.
authors: England GCW, Newcombe JR
abstract: Persistent mating-induced endometritis commonly causes subfertility in mares. We assessed 313 natural-cover breeding cycles from 192 mares examined daily until at least day 5 after ovulation, establishing the last day post-ovulation on which uterine fluid remained detectable. Fluid was detected after ovulation in 52.4% of all cycles. The longer fluid persisted the lower the pregnancy rate: 73.8% with no post-ovulation fluid, 32.0% when fluid was last detected on day 2 post-ovulation, and 17.6% when fluid persisted to day 3 or beyond. Each additional day fluid persisted post-ovulation was associated with a 41% reduction in the odds of pregnancy. Recording fluid duration relative to ovulation was superior in predicting pregnancy compared with recording fluid duration relative to mating. Data from a subsequent cycle were available for 101 mares bred again at cycle 2 (97 that did not conceive at cycle 1 and 4 that had lost a cycle 1 pregnancy); attempts were made to mate the mare earlier in subsequent cycles. Total number of days fluid was detectable from mating was similar at cycle 1 and cycle 2 in these mares (1.88 versus 1.86 days; P = 0.77). In 54 mares the day of mating at the next cycle relative to ovulation was advanced by at least one day at cycle 2; and yet the duration of fluid persistence remained unchanged. Consequently, the last day of fluid persistence post-ovulation decreased (1.61 to 0.65 days; P < 0.001). In the 47 mares whose mating interval was unchanged at cycle 2, the last post-ovulation fluid day was also unchanged, providing an internal control for the redistribution finding. Earlier mating was associated with higher pregnancy rates across all cycles (OR 1.969; P < 0.001) but not significantly when only first-cycles were analysed (P = 0.92), or after adjustment for cycle number (P = 0.69). Persistence of fluid post-ovulation is negatively associated with pregnancy rate, with a critical reduction when fluid persists beyond day 2. In treated mares, total fluid duration appeared to be a fixed characteristic; earlier mating redistributed the period of fluid persistence to earlier relative to ovulation, resulting in fewer post-ovulation fluid days. Plausibly, earlier fluid resolution after ovulation may allow better uterine recovery prior to entry of the embryo and thus increase pregnancy rate.

title: Effect of short-term storage prior to vitrification on pregnancy rates of dromedary camel embryos.
authors: Mulligan BP, Skidmore JA
abstract: Short-term storage of embryos prior to cryopreservation may improve the logistical flexibility of dromedary camel embryo transfer (ET) programs. However, the impact of such storage on embryo cryotolerance remains unclear. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the effect of storing dromedary camel embryos for 24 h at either room temperature (RT) or 4 °C prior to vitrification on subsequent pregnancy rates following ET. A total of 60 Day-7 in vivo-derived embryos were assigned to one of three treatment groups: immediate vitrification without prior storage (NS, n = 20), storage at 4 °C for 24 h prior to vitrification (4C, n = 20), or storage at room temperature (RT, n = 20) for 24 h prior to vitrification. Within each group, embryos were further categorised according to diameter (<500 μm or ≥500 μm). Following warming, embryos were transferred in pairs to synchronized recipients and pregnancy establishment was assessed between days 18-20 and day 60 of gestation. The transfer of NS embryos produced pregnancy rates of 60% (6/10) at 18-20 days and 50% (5/10) at day 60. Transfer of embryos in the 4C group resulted in pregnancy rates of 40% (4/10) and 30% (3/10), respectively. In contrast, embryos stored at RT prior to vitrification failed to establish pregnancies (0/10). These findings demonstrate that while short-term cooling may be compatible with subsequent vitrification, storage at room temperature could severely compromise embryo cryotolerance.
